newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee seen overvalued,in need of correction.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee seen overvalued,in need of correction.

text.p: The Indian rupee is overvalued and in need of an immediate correction, securities firm Crosby Securities said in a research report.
"The rupee is overvalued at its current exchange rate of 35.7 per dollar," Crosby said in its South Asia Economic Review published on Wednesday.
Crosby said it expected the rupee, which opened on Thursday at 35.72/73 per dollar, to weaken to 37.7 per dollar by end-March 1997 and further to 39.6 by end-March 1998.

"The rupee's real effective exchange rate suggests that, to keep Indian exports competitive, by compensating inflation differentials with her export competitor nations, the currency has to depreciate to 36.6 rupees to a dollar immediately."
Crosby said India was expected to make $14 billion worth of debt service payments in 1996/97. "We expect much of this to be bunched in November 1996-January 1997," the review said.
"Since India's forex markets are notoriously shallow, these repayments are likely to cause volatility during this period," it said.
